hook: Skipping your 401(k) match is like turning down a raise.

blocks.narration: Skipping your 401(k) match is like turning down a raise. Many American employers add money when you save. Plenty of workers leave it unclaimed.
blocks.visual: Young office worker at a desk pushes away a glowing envelope stamped with a dollar sign, coworkers in the background, slow push-in

blocks.narration: Here is how it works. If your company matches fifty percent up to six percent, saving six percent gets you three percent extra.
blocks.visual: Two stacks of coins grow side by side on a paycheck, the second stack labeled 'match' rises halfway as fast, bold numbers 6% and 3% pop in

blocks.narration: On a sixty thousand dollar salary, that is eighteen hundred dollars a year. Check your benefits portal. Follow for one money rule a day.
blocks.visual: Calendar pages flip while a jar labeled 'retirement' fills with coins, ending on a phone screen showing a benefits portal checkbox being ticked

cta: Follow for one money rule a day.
visual_style: clean editorial collage, warm paper textures, bold numbers, green and cream palette

captions.hook_line: Your 401(k) match is a raise you might be skipping 💸
captions.body: If your employer matches contributions, saving at least up to the match is the easiest return you'll ever get. Look up your plan's match formula today.
